title: ThruLines #006
phrase: The voice of my generation. Or at least a voice.

questions.subject: Music
questions.prompt: Who was the drummer for Bad Company?
questions.connectionNote: Kirke — as in his daughter Jemima Kirke, the show's Jessa.

questions.subject: News
questions.prompt: Which news anchor was suspended for falsely claiming his helicopter was hit in Iraq?
questions.connectionNote: Williams — as in his daughter Allison Williams, the show's Marnie.

questions.subject: Theater
questions.prompt: Which Pulitzer-winning playwright wrote Glengarry Glen Ross?
questions.connectionNote: Mamet — as in his daughter Zosia Mamet, the show's Shoshanna.

questions.subject: Celebrity
questions.prompt: What is the first name of David and Victoria Beckham's eldest son?
questions.connectionNote: Brooklyn — the borough where the whole show lives.

questions.subject: Comedy
questions.prompt: What's the last name of the Blue Collar Comedy Tour's famous ventriloquist?
questions.connectionNote: Dunham — as in Lena Dunham, who created the show and said the line.

reveal.summary: Girls. A drummer, an anchor, a playwright, a Beckham and a ventriloquist — and four of the five answers are the famous parents (and one borough) behind the cast: Simon Kirke (Jemima), Brian Williams (Allison), David Mamet (Zosia), Lena Dunham's namesake in comedy, and Brooklyn itself. The line is Hannah Horvath's all-time hedge, from the pilot.
reveal.ohMoment: The answers were the parents all along — the most famous surnames in the credits, hiding in plain sight.

editorial.notes: Signature construction: every answer is a cast member's famous relative (plus the borough). Phrase trimmed to the hedge's spine (37 letters) per the shorter-phrase doctrine: aim 18-35 letters, ceiling ~40.
